openClinicalQuestions: Dr. Zalak: refine patient-facing wording on abdominal doming so it does not overstate harm from every visible midline change, while still prompting assessment when symptoms or load intolerance appear.

claimLedger.claim: After straightforward birth, gentle exercise (walking, stretches, pelvic floor) when ready; usually get advice at 6-week check before high-impact; longer recovery and talk to midwife/GP before strenuous activity after complicated birth or caesarean; swimming after bleeding stopped 7 days.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Keeping fit and healthy with a baby · Media last reviewed 2 August 2026
claimLedger.limitations: UK NHS pathway; Indian postnatal follow-up timing may differ

claimLedger.claim: Postnatal check at 6–8 weeks reviews recovery and invites discussion of continence, perineal pain and related concerns; not framed as sport clearance.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Your 6-week postnatal check · Page last reviewed 9 October 2026

claimLedger.claim: Suggests low-impact focus in first 3 postnatal months and return to running 3–6 months at earliest; designed to assist clinical reasoning, not prescribe one path.
claimLedger.sourceSection: Goom, Donnelly & Brockwell · Returning to running postnatal – guidelines for medical, health and fitness professionals · Published March 2019
claimLedger.limitations: Expert consensus / limited direct evidence; for professionals managing runners
